microsoft-onelake:rest-spec-support:curr.notes: OneLake table APIs expose an IRC-compatible endpoint (onelake.table.fabric.microsoft.com/iceberg) limited to read-only metadata operations: get config, list/get namespaces and list/get tables.
caveats: No write endpoints: tables can't be created or committed over IRC
No view endpoints and no spec credential vending (clients authenticate with Entra ID storage tokens)

microsoft-onelake:v2-spec-support:curren.notes: Iceberg tables in OneLake, written directly (e.g. by Snowflake) or virtualized from Delta Lake, use format v2; the Delta-Iceberg metadata virtualization supports v2 today.
caveats: Virtualization converts only the latest metadata version and requires fewer than 5,000 commits on the source table

microsoft-onelake:v3-spec-support:curren.notes: The table-format virtualization supports Iceberg v2 only; Microsoft states that reading Iceberg v3 tables is being worked on.

microsoft-onelake:serves-own-irc:current.notes: Read-only IRC on its own managed OneLake tables (GET/HEAD metadata endpoints with Entra OAuth); no IRC write or commit, and reads rely on the consumer's own storage access rather than spec credential vending.

microsoft-onelake:rw-foreign-irc:current.notes: External Iceberg is read via OneLake shortcuts and metadata virtualization, not via IRC, and there is no IRC write.

microsoft-onelake:federation-broker:curr.notes: Multi-source shortcuts (S3, GCS, ADLS, Dataverse) broker storage rather than catalog IRC: there is no IRC client, so this is not spec-compliant IRC federation.

microsoft-onelake:multi-engine-multi-clo.notes: External engines such as Snowflake, DuckDB and PyIceberg can read its Iceberg over the IRC endpoint, and Snowflake can write to OneLake storage via an external volume (not IRC); compute is otherwise Fabric-centric.

microsoft-onelake:governance-cred-vendin.notes: Microsoft Purview provides sensitivity labels and DLP, but it is Fabric-only and not enforced over IRC.
